question: What does a graceful (controlled) Kafka broker shutdown do that a hard kill does not?
reference:
It syncs all logs to disk, so no log recovery is needed on restart, and it moves leadership of the broker's partitions to other replicas before shutting down, so each partition is unavailable for only a few milliseconds.
Source: https://kafka.apache.org/43/operations/basic-kafka-operations/#graceful-shutdown

question: Which setting enables controlled leadership migration on shutdown?
reference:
controlled.shutdown.enable=true
Source: https://kafka.apache.org/43/operations/basic-kafka-operations/#graceful-shutdown

question: When does a controlled shutdown fail?
reference:
It only succeeds if every partition on the broker has replicas elsewhere: replication factor greater than 1 and at least one of those replicas alive.
Source: https://kafka.apache.org/43/operations/basic-kafka-operations/#graceful-shutdown

question: After restarting a broker, it leads no partitions. How do I restore preferred leadership if auto.leader.rebalance.enable is false?
reference:
Run bin/kafka-leader-election.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 --election-type preferred --all-topic-partitions.
Source: https://kafka.apache.org/43/operations/basic-kafka-operations/#balancing-leadership

question: For a partition with replica list 1,5,9, which broker is the preferred leader?
reference:
Broker 1, because it is first in the replica list.
Source: https://kafka.apache.org/43/operations/basic-kafka-operations/#balancing-leadership

question: How do I see the current KRaft quorum leader and voters?
reference:
bin/kafka-metadata-quorum.sh --bootstrap-server localhost:9092 describe --status. It shows LeaderId, LeaderEpoch, HighWatermark, MaxFollowerLag, CurrentVoters and CurrentObservers.
Source: https://kafka.apache.org/43/operations/kraft/#metadata-quorum-tool

question: How do I decode records in the KRaft metadata log?
reference:
bin/kafka-dump-log.sh --cluster-metadata-decoder --files <path to a __cluster_metadata-0 .log segment or .checkpoint snapshot>.
Source: https://kafka.apache.org/43/operations/kraft/#dump-log-tool

question: Which snapshot file must not be used with kafka-metadata-shell.sh?
reference:
00000000000000000000-0000000000.checkpoint, because it contains no cluster metadata. Use a valid snapshot file.
Source: https://kafka.apache.org/43/operations/kraft/#metadata-shell

question: What values can the KRaft 'Current State' metric take?
reference:
leader, candidate, voted, follower, unattached, observer.
Source: https://kafka.apache.org/43/operations/monitoring/#kraft-quorum-monitoring-metrics

question: What does a value of -1 for the Current Leader raft metric mean?
reference:
The current quorum leader is unknown.
Source: https://kafka.apache.org/43/operations/monitoring/#kraft-quorum-monitoring-metrics

question: Where does Strimzi store the progress of a running Cruise Control rebalance?
reference:
In a ConfigMap with the same name as the KafkaRebalance resource, referenced by status.progress.rebalanceProgressConfigMap. It is updated on each reconciliation of the KafkaRebalance.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-tracking-cluster-rebalance-str

question: How do I get the estimated time to completion of a running rebalance?
reference:
kubectl get configmaps <my_rebalance> -o jsonpath="{['data']['estimatedTimeToCompletionInMinutes']}"
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-tracking-cluster-rebalance-str

question: What does completedByteMovementPercentage show?
reference:
The percentage of data movement completed, in bytes, as an integer from 0 to 100 rounded down.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-tracking-cluster-rebalance-str

question: How do I stop a running Cruise Control rebalance in Strimzi?
reference:
Annotate the KafkaRebalance with strimzi.io/rebalance="stop" and wait until the status changes to Stopped. Cruise Control finishes the current batch of reassignments first.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-stopping-cluster-rebalance-str

question: Does stopping a rebalance roll back the partition moves already made?
reference:
No. Completed reassignments stay applied, so the cluster state differs from before the rebalance. Performance in this stopped state might be worse than at the start. For further rebalancing, generate a new proposal.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-stopping-cluster-rebalance-str

question: What does 'Failed to acquire lock lock::myproject::Kafka::my-cluster within 10000ms' in the Cluster Operator log mean?
reference:
Acquiring the per-cluster operation lock took longer than STRIMZI_OPERATION_TIMEOUT_MS, so the operator logged a DEBUG message. The timed-out operation is retried at the next periodic reconciliation.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#con-failed-lock-warnings-str

question: How often are operations that timed out on lock acquisition retried?
reference:
At the next periodic reconciliation, whose interval is STRIMZI_FULL_RECONCILIATION_INTERVAL_MS. The default is 120 seconds.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#con-failed-lock-warnings-str

question: The INFO message 'Reconciliation is in progress' keeps repeating with the same reconciliation number. What could it mean and what does Strimzi suggest?
reference:
It might indicate a lock release error. Restarting the Cluster Operator can resolve it.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#con-failed-lock-warnings-str

question: Why does the Cluster Operator use locks?
reference:
To make sure only one operation runs at a time for each cluster. Operations such as cluster creation, rolling updates, scaling down and scaling up are covered. An operation that starts while the lock is held waits for the current one to finish.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#con-failed-lock-warnings-str

question: At what log level is the lock-timeout message written?
reference:
DEBUG, for example: DEBUG AbstractOperator:406 - Reconciliation #55(timer) Kafka(myproject/my-cluster): Failed to acquire lock ... within 10000ms.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#con-failed-lock-warnings-str

question: How do I trigger a rolling restart of a single Kafka pod managed by Strimzi?
reference:
Annotate the pod with strimzi.io/manual-rolling-update="true". The procedure's example is kubectl annotate pod <cluster_name>-kafka-<index_number> strimzi.io/manual-rolling-update="true", but with node pools (required for KRaft) Kafka pods are named <kafka_cluster_name>-<pool_name>-<pod_id>, so use the pod's actual name. Then wait for the next reconciliation (every two minutes by default).
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-manual-rolling-update-pods-str

question: How do I know a manual rolling update of a pod has completed?
reference:
The strimzi.io/manual-rolling-update annotation is removed from the pod automatically when its rolling update is complete.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-manual-rolling-update-pods-str

question: Should I annotate the StrimziPodSet or the pods for a manual rolling update?
reference:
Annotating a StrimziPodSet rolls all its pods, but if the operator is reconciling it at that moment the annotation can be overwritten without a restart. To avoid this race, Strimzi recommends annotating the individual pods.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-manual-rolling-update-strimzipodset-str

question: What topic configuration keeps Kafka available during a rolling update?
reference:
Replication factor of at least 3 and min.insync.replicas one less than the replication factor, for example replicas: 3 and min.insync.replicas: 2, on a highly available cluster.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-manual-rolling-update-pods-str

question: If the manual rolling update fails, does the reconciliation stop?
reference:
No. The reconciliation continues, so the Cluster Operator can recover from some fixable problems later in it, for example by recreating a missing PVC or PV that made the update fail.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-manual-rolling-update-pods-str

question: What is the StrimziPodSet name for a Kafka Connect cluster called my-connect-cluster?
reference:
my-connect-cluster-connect.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-manual-rolling-update-strimzipodset-str

question: How do I restart a MirrorMaker 2 connector in Strimzi?
reference:
Annotate the KafkaMirrorMaker2 resource with the connector name: kubectl annotate KafkaMirrorMaker2 <mirrormaker_cluster_name> "strimzi.io/restart-connector=<mirrormaker_connector_name>".
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-manual-restart-mirrormaker2-connector-str

question: How do I pass includeTasks and onlyFailed when restarting a MirrorMaker 2 connector?
reference:
Append them after a colon: "strimzi.io/restart-connector=source-cluster->target-cluster.MirrorCheckpointConnector:includeTasks,onlyFailed".
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-manual-restart-mirrormaker2-connector-str

question: What annotation restarts a single MirrorMaker 2 connector task?
reference:
strimzi.io/restart-connector-task=<mirrormaker_connector_name>:<task_id> on the KafkaMirrorMaker2 resource.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-manual-restart-mirrormaker2-connector-task-str

question: Can I use strimzi.io/restart on a KafkaMirrorMaker2 resource like on a KafkaConnector?
reference:
No. MirrorMaker 2 uses strimzi.io/restart-connector and strimzi.io/restart-connector-task on the KafkaMirrorMaker2 resource. strimzi.io/restart and strimzi.io/restart-task are for KafkaConnector resources.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-manual-restart-mirrormaker2-connector-str

question: What does the example MirrorMaker 2 Grafana dashboard show about tasks?
reference:
The number of tasks, replication latency and offset synchronization latency.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#checking_connector_task_operations

question: How do I view the Topic Operator logs in a Strimzi deployment?
reference:
Read the topic-operator container of the Entity Operator. Its pod has a generated name (<kafka_cluster_name>-entity-operator-<random_string>), so select it through the Deployment, for example: kubectl logs -n kafka deployment/my-cluster-entity-operator -c topic-operator.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-configuring-entity-operator-watched-namespace-str

question: Where is the Strimzi Cluster Operator logging configuration stored?
reference:
In a ConfigMap named strimzi-cluster-operator, created with defaults at install time and defined in install/cluster-operator/050-ConfigMap-strimzi-cluster-operator.yaml.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#ref-operator-cluster-logging-configmap-str

question: How often does the Cluster Operator reload its logging configuration, and can I remove that setting?
reference:
monitorInterval sets the reload interval in seconds; the default is 30. Do not remove monitorInterval from the ConfigMap.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#ref-operator-cluster-logging-configmap-str

question: What happens to Cluster Operator logging if the strimzi-cluster-operator ConfigMap is deleted after deployment?
reference:
The most recently loaded logging configuration stays in effect. To load a new configuration, create a new ConfigMap.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#ref-operator-cluster-logging-configmap-str

question: Is kubectl logs enough for production log collection with Strimzi?
reference:
The docs describe kubectl logs as a tool for direct, real-time debugging of recent pod logs. For production they recommend a persistent, Kubernetes-supported cluster-level logging architecture that collects logs from all components.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#con-using-loggers_str

question: My KafkaTopic shows NotReady with reason PartitionDecreaseException. What is wrong and how do I fix it?
reference:
The partition count was decreased in the KafkaTopic, which Kafka does not support ('Number of partitions cannot be decreased'). Reset spec.partitions to the original value; the status then shows the topic as ready.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-configuring-kafka-topic-str

question: Which KafkaTopic changes does the Topic Operator not allow?
reference:
Renaming the topic in spec.topicName (a spec.topicName/status.topicName mismatch is detected), decreasing spec.partitions, and modifying spec.replicas. Changing replicas requires Cruise Control.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-configuring-kafka-topic-str

question: Two KafkaTopic resources point at the same Kafka topic. Which one wins?
reference:
The resource created first manages the topic. The newer resources get a conflict in their status and their Ready status is set to False.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#con-operator-topic-names-str

question: The Topic Operator is down and KafkaTopic deletion hangs, leaving the namespace stuck terminating. What can I do?
reference:
Remove the finalizers, for example kubectl get kt <topic_name> -o=json | jq '.metadata.finalizers = null' | kubectl apply -f -. Be aware that if the Topic Operator is not running, the Kafka topic itself will not be deleted.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#con-removing-topic-finalizers-str

question: I changed a managed topic's config directly in Kafka with kafka-configs. Will the change stay?
reference:
No. Changes go only from the KafkaTopic to Kafka, and changes made to a managed topic outside the KafkaTopic are reverted.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#con-application-topic-handling-str

question: Where do I look when the READY column of a KafkaTopic stays blank?
reference:
In the status message of the resource YAML (kubectl get kafkatopics <name> -o yaml) or in the Topic Operator logs.
Source: https://strimzi.io/docs/operators/1.3.1/deploying#proc-configuring-kafka-topic-str
